Figure 1: A passing full arrangement on one validation scene. (a) and (b) are matched Blender renders of the
recorded source and predicted poses. (c) draws each footprint twice: a dashed outline at the source and a filled
shape at the prediction. Arrows connect centers and are not robot trajectories. The model is given the original
overhead RGB, not these presentation renders.
Abstract. We study language-guided knolling from overhead RGB to planar target poses. The goal
is end-to-end learning; the implemented system uses staged neural training and explicit geometric
decoding. On 128 sealed families and 640 image–instruction pairs, v2 achieves 540/640 strict
successes (84.4%), versus 489/640 (76.4%) with the same learned base. The paired gain is 8.0
percentage points (family-bootstrap 95% interval: 4.8–11.6), preserving all previous successes.
Spacing violations affect 71 of 100 remaining failures. A broader joint-training pilot failed; stable
joint learning and physical execution remain open objectives.
1
INTRODUCTION
Knolling organizes objects into aligned, evenly spaced layouts for tasks such as assembly preparation.
Visual neatness is insufficient: moving an unselected object, missing a gap, or crossing a region
1

boundary invalidates an instruction. We ask: How reliably can an RGB-and-language system satisfy
all arrangement constraints at once?
The system supports two to eight procedural objects and English commands for full arrangement,
color-selective placement, and preservation, without teacher poses or layouts at inference. We
contribute an object-centric pipeline with selective preservation, a family-separated evaluation, and
complete-task failure analysis. The paired release comparison evaluates an inference-refinement
bundle over a fixed learned base.
Related work.
Knolling Bot learns tidy placements (Hu et al., 2025); its graspability extension
addresses clutter (Hu et al., 2023). This course project’s “v2” is distinct from that published extension.
StructFormer predicts language-guided arrangements (Liu et al., 2022), while Transporter Networks
and CLIPort predict manipulation actions (Zeng et al., 2021; Shridhar et al., 2022). Our restricted
RGB-to-layout task evaluates complete geometric validity; their hardware results and metrics are not
directly comparable.

Figure 2: The hybrid system and its learned layout core. Contextual features select rows and pointer order; pose
heads read the original relation features. Neural modules are learned in stages, while explicit rules constrain and
repair predictions. The global goal g is text-only; object features condition separate referent selection m. Token
and row glyphs are schematic.
Perception and language grounding.
RT-DETR-R18 (Zhao et al., 2024), from the DETR family
(Carion et al., 2020), supplies queries and physical attributes. Crop-conditioned appearance and
size heads refine each detection. Retained objects form 12-dimensional vectors of position, size,
angle, color, and shape. MiniLM (Wang et al., 2020; Reimers & Gurevych, 2020) supplies text
tokens to seven learned goal queries, producing a 13-dimensional global goal. A separate object–
language attention branch predicts per-object selection. Explicit English templates correct disagreeing
region/gap bins.
Learned structure and constrained coordinates.
A relation encoder produces 128-dimensional
features. Four-head set attention guides row membership and autoregressive within-row order;
coordinate heads retain the original features. Structures are ranked by row/order log-probabilities,
with at most eight candidates checked per constrained search. Predicted area determines size order.
The decoder uses rotated envelopes and ±2 mm gap bands. Conditional row repair and color splitting
propose alternatives when needed. An unsuccessful bounded repair retains the original prediction;
feasibility is not guaranteed.
Selective preservation.
Partial placement selects the named color and searches translations around
held objects. Held/no-op centers use detections; angles use RGB silhouette principal-component
analysis with a learned fallback. Preservation therefore requires accurate perception. Appendix A
specifies routing and search bounds.
3

3
DATA, TRAINING, AND EVALUATION
Synthetic corpus.
The generated corpus contains 4,000 geometry families and 20,000 image–
instruction pairs. Each family shares one RGB image across five instructions: three full arrangements,
one color-selective task, and one no-op. Procedural boxes, chamfers, and capsules have red, green,
or blue appearances. A geometric teacher generates layouts, and an independent validator checks
them before acceptance. Images are rendered with Blender Cycles. The fixed split is 3,200/400/400
families, or 16,000/2,000/2,000 pairs, for train/validation/test. Splitting by family prevents identical
source images from crossing these pools. The 20,000 figure is corpus size, not the exposure of every
training stage.
Staged optimization.
Perception and arrangement bases are trained separately. Subsequent relation
stages use a 791-pair train manifest and 94-pair validation manifest. A size-residual stage uses
source-dimension supervision. Restricted joint fine-tuning then updates only the size residual and
selected row-coordinate parameters; perception, language, goal, relation, row assignment, order,
and angle heads remain frozen. Refined sizes are detached before the pose computation, so pose
loss does not train perception. The selector trains row and pointer cross-entropies on 5,085 usable
full-arrangement pairs from 5,376 eligible pairs (1,792 train families); 291 pairs fail detection-count
or association checks. Eight epochs are recorded, with epoch 1 selected using 1,200 full validation
pairs. Losses, hyperparameters, gradient boundaries, and historical diagnostics appear in Appendix B.
A broader joint-training pilot was attempted but rejected after collapse: at update 200, success fell
from 2/38 to 0/38 on development and from 24/152 to 1/152 on validation. This observation motivated
retaining the stable staged system. It is one unsuccessful configuration, not evidence that end-to-end
training is impossible.
Sealed release comparison.
The final evaluation uses a later, separately generated set of 128
families and 640 pairs. Family IDs, RGB hashes, and asset-family IDs are disjoint from the 20,000-
pair corpus. Its objects use the development asset pool not rendered in the 20,000-pair corpus, within
the same procedural shape/color vocabulary. The recorded modes are 384 full, 127 partial, and 129
no-op pairs. Both releases were scored on these same records with the same evaluator and threshold.
Neither this set nor the official 2,000-pair test split was used to select v2 checkpoints or thresholds.
This paper reaggregates the stored sealed scores; it does not rerun inference or select a new model on
them.
Strict complete-scene success.
A count mismatch immediately fails. Otherwise Hungarian match-
ing associates predicted source objects with true identities; each association must meet a 10 mm
center-error limit and envelope IoU ≥0.5. Target poses are then checked using true object geometry.
Every applicable constraint must pass: selection/preservation, requested region, axis, row alignment,
gaps, color grouping, size order, collision, clearance, and boundary. The score is the mean binary
scene outcome,

RESULTS AND ANALYSIS
A paired improvement with the learned base fixed.
Table 2 compares releases with unchanged
learned architecture and checkpoint-loading paths. V2 adds 10 mm duplicate suppression, sentence-
consistent region/gap choices, stricter named-color selection, and feasibility-gated row/color repair. It
evaluates this inference bundle over the same learned base, rather than additional training or isolated
component effects.

V2 retains all 489 v1 successes and gains 51: 24 full, 20 partial, and 7 no-op scenes. Failures fall
from 151 to 100, a 33.8% relative reduction. Because five instructions share each image, uncertainty
is estimated by resampling paired families, not individual pairs. Across 10,000 bootstrap resamples
(seed 20261112), the 95% percentile interval for the improvement is +4.8 to +11.6 percentage points.
Twenty-nine families improve, 99 tie, and none worsen. This interval describes variation across
evaluation families conditional on the frozen systems; it does not cover training-seed uncertainty or
real-world domain shift.

count grows; bins contain 90 or 95 pairs. (b) Error tags overlap: a scene may fail more than one check. The
seven shown categories include every nonzero v2 error category; Appendix C lists all v1 categories.
What improved, and what remains difficult?
Partial tasks show the largest gain. Count failures
fall from 45 to 5, and region failures from 17 to 4. These changes are consistent with the added rules,
but do not identify their individual causal contributions. Eight-object success rises from 47/90 to
65/90 (52.2% to 72.2%), remaining below the two-object bin (91/95 for both).
Spacing remains the main weakness: 49 horizontal-gap and 42 vertical-gap failures overlap in 20
scenes, affecting 71 of the 100 failures. Other tags are 11 size-order, 7 clearance, 5 count, 4 region,
and 4 preservation errors. Internal feasibility uses predicted dimensions; scoring uses true rectangles.
Thus internally valid geometry can still miss the gap threshold. This identifies a plausible failure
mechanism, not a root-cause frequency established by the tags.

Figure 4: Object-level motion in the eight-object validation example. Dashed footprints mark recorded source
poses and solid outlines mark saved predictions, in a common world frame. Matched IDs and straight
center-displacement arrows establish correspondence. The ledger shows translations and signed, 180◦-periodic
long-axis rotations; its glyphs compare source and target axes. Arrows are not robot trajectories.
Valid tasks require more than tidy appearance.
Figures 6–7 locate the violations in a separate
three-command example. Its full-layout row gap exceeds the allowed upper limit by 0.657 mm. The
partial-layout clearance misses the tolerance-adjusted minimum by only 3.9 µm: a borderline score
failure, not a visible collision. This distinction exposes sensitivity to geometric estimates and scoring
thresholds; it does not establish real-world positioning precision. Complete-scene validity also need
not track local selector accuracy (Appendix B).
End-to-end scope.
RGB and English produce poses without teacher information at inference.
Staged losses, discrete selection, template correction, image-based angle estimation, and geometry
remain essential; successful joint training is unproven. No real-image, paraphrase, severe-occlusion,
or physical evaluation is available. Static clearance is not a safe manipulation sequence.
Evidence limits.
Evaluation covers a calibrated synthetic domain with three colors/shape types and
at most eight objects, using one learned base without factorial ablation or multiple seeds. The 0.137 s
median inference time is not a deployment benchmark. Missing historical trainers and undistributed
checkpoints prevent exact retraining; the package reproduces the paper’s analysis and visualization.
6
CONCLUSION
Knolling Bot v2 achieves 84.4% strict scene success, improving by 8.0 points over its predecessor on
a sealed, family-separated set. The results support a staged hybrid system where identity, instruction
consistency, and geometry jointly determine success. Next steps are dimension-sensitive spacing,
controlled ablations, stable joint optimization, and physical validation.
6

Constraint handling and preservation.
The geometry decoder uses rotated rectangle corners,
not a silhouette-derived width. Regions are full (.02, .02, .58, .38), left (.02, .02, .28, .38), and right
(.32, .02, .58, .38), in metres. It anchors row centers within the feasible region and may move a
fitting layout 1 mm inward when space allows. Ranking alternatives by neural probabilities does not
guarantee that the globally best feasible arrangement is examined. Row-partition enumeration can
consider more structures before returning up to eight proposals.
For a uniquely classified named color, partial mode replaces the moving set with those objects. Held
objects constrain the static placement. The bounded clearance search translates the moving block on
8

a 5 mm grid within ±120 mm. It is not a grasp or trajectory planner. Held/no-op angle estimation
uses connected components in a local ±80 mm image window, a chroma threshold of 25/255, at
least 40 pixels, and the principal axis of the silhouette. A direction head supplies fallback orientation.
This PCA correction already exists in v1 and must not be credited as a new v2 improvement.
Version-controlled change.
The v1.0.0–v2.0.0 delta changes only inference: duplicate suppression,
sentence-consistent region/gap choices, exact named-color mover replacement, infeasible-row repair,
and feasible color-row splitting. Learned architecture, loading paths, set attention, size residual,
constraint search, and PCA correction are shared; individual effects remain unmeasured.

Development evidence and its limits.
The saved 152-scene full-arrangement diagnostic improves
from 24 to 42 successes after size refinement and from 42 to 54 after restricted joint tuning. Size
refinement reduces median major-dimension error from 1.419 to 0.790 mm (796 matched objects),
while restricted joint tuning reduces median vertical-gap error from 2.015 to 1.588 mm. These
are recorded development stages with evolving code and selection gates, not independent final-test
ablations. In contrast, the broader joint pilot falls from 2/38 to 0/38 development successes and from
24/152 to 1/152 validation successes at update 200; the best checkpoint remains update 0. A historical
260-scene diagnostic overlapped earlier fitting data and is excluded from claims of independent
generalization.

DATA AND STATISTICAL DETAILS
Scene and asset seeds are 120912 and 120913, respectively. Major dimensions span 40–80 mm, minor
dimensions 25–50 mm, and heights 5–20 mm on a 1 mm grid, with aspect ratio ≥1.3. The corpus
uses continuous_rows_v3 teacher layouts and english_rows_v1 instructions. For family i,
bucket ⌊i/20⌋mod 10 assigns 0–7 to train, 8 to validation, and 9 to test. Source clearance/margin
is 12 mm; accepted targets require 10 mm and exact source copies for locked poses. Independent
validation checks targets. Dataset RGB rendering used Blender 5.1.0, Cycles CPU, and 32 samples;
PNG bytes may vary across environments.
The separate final set uses scene seed 20261112, registry seed 120913, and development assets.
Its 128 families/640 pairs share no geometry-family IDs, RGB hashes, or asset-family IDs with
the corpus. This tests new instances within the procedural domain. Mode labels follow teacher
outcomes: already-satisfied color-selective commands become no-op. Actual mode counts determine
denominators.

Why the borderline example matters.
The partial result is not evidence of a visually poor
arrangement or a physical collision. Its failure is a precise consequence of the synthetic evaluator’s
envelope-distance threshold. True mesh silhouettes and oriented bounding rectangles differ, especially
for capsules and chamfers; the annotated quantity is rectangle-to-rectangle clearance. This example
motivates distinguishing failure severity and scoring margins from a binary success rate. It supplies
no estimate of how frequently such near-threshold cases occur across the holdout.
Pose and geometry fidelity.
Every presentation image renders a preserved scene record. Meshes
extrude the project’s original footprint polygons to their recorded heights, retaining identity, color,
dimensions and source/predicted pose. No layout is adjusted for composition. Before/after views
share orthographic camera, illumination, materials, background, and image quality. Blender 5.1.0
uses Cycles CPU, 1920 × 1280 resolution, denoising and adaptive sampling with a 128-sample
maximum. Overhead closeups use the same materials and lighting with a calibrated camera.
The original 576 × 384 RGB images remain the actual inference inputs (one appears in Figure 2);
presentation renders are generated only afterward. Input/output hashes, object transforms, camera
settings, editable Blender scenes and scripts are included. An independent check reopens every
saved scene and compares all object transforms and mesh vertices with the source records. The only
residual differences are float32 storage quantization, below 10−7 in the corresponding meter/radian
coordinates. No additional model inference or training is performed.

REPRODUCIBILITY AND EVIDENCE PACKAGE
The analysis compares v1.0.0 (26dca53) and v2.0.0 (593bd5d); the release-candidate measurement
was carried forward without changing inference. Manuscript preparation used checkout 535f14f.
The adopted entry points are load_adopted in the end-to-end scorer and poses_from_detection
in size_refinement.py. Source-identity matching minimizes a Hungarian cost incorporating
confidence, source position, size, and angle. Each match must additionally satisfy center distance
≤10 mm and oriented-envelope IoU ≥0.5; otherwise the scene fails with source_identity.
Target poses then undergo the independent semantic and geometry checks.
The model runtime uses Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1, torchvision 0.24.1, and transformers 4.57.3.
Pretrained snapshots are pinned in configs/pretrained_rtdetr.json. Reloading requires
local base/parent checkpoints, relation, joint row/size and selector weights, selection/direction heads,
and pretrained caches. The source repository does not distribute these weights or datasets, and the
historical selector trainer and independent-set generator are absent. The package below supports
reproduction of the paper’s analysis and figures, rather than claiming full training reproduction.

Compute scope.
The selector stage records 1,719 GPU-seconds, not the total project compute.
Saved timing gives median 131.5/137.2 ms and mean 169.2/197.5 ms for v1/v2. Hardware, warmup,
and serving conditions are not controlled sufficiently for a throughput claim. No total training budget,
deployment cost, or physical cycle time is established.
Rebuilding.
The README provides commands and dependency pins. The two analysis scripts in
Table 6 reconstruct the statistics and seven figures. Running latexmk -pdf main.tex compiles
the manuscript. All figure PDFs are included, so compilation alone requires neither Python nor a
GPU, checkpoints, or the original datasets.
Assistance disclosure.
Codex assisted with repository and record inspection, primary-source
literature discovery, drafting, figure scripting, and LaTeX typesetting. Experimental outcomes come
from saved project records. Manuscript preparation performed statistical reaggregation and Blender
visualization at fixed saved poses, without generating additional model predictions or training results.
